cystic mastitis.synonyms: fibrocystic breast disease; fibrocystic disease of the breast; cystic breast disease

cystine.definition: a crystalline amino acid found in proteins (especially keratin); discovered in bladder stones

cystitis.definition: inflammation of the urinary bladder and ureters

cystocele.definition: hernia in which the urinary bladder protrudes through the wall of the vagina; sometimes occurs after childbirth

cystoid macular edema.definition: a specific pattern of swelling in the central retina

cystolith.definition: a calculus formed in the bladder

cystophora cristata.definition: medium-sized blackish-grey seal with large inflatable sac on the head; of Arctic and northern Atlantic waters

cystopteris bulbifera.definition: North American fern often bearing bulbils on the leaflets
cystopteris bulbifera.synonyms: bulblet fern; bulblet bladder fern; berry fern

cystopteris fragilis.definition: delicate fern widely distributed in North America and European having thin pinnatifid fronds with brittle stems
cystopteris fragilis.synonyms: brittle bladder fern; brittle fern; fragile fern

cystopteris montana.definition: fern of rocky mountainous areas of hemisphere

cytesis proliferus.definition: shrub of Canary Islands having bristle-tipped oblanceolate leaves; used as cattle fodder

cytidine.definition: a nucleoside component of RNA; composed of cytosine and a ribose ring

cytisus albus.definition: low European broom having trifoliate leaves and yellowish-white flowers
cytisus albus.synonyms: white broom; white Spanish broom; Cytisus multiflorus

cytisus multiflorus.definition: low European broom having trifoliate leaves and yellowish-white flowers
cytisus multiflorus.synonyms: white broom; white Spanish broom; Cytisus albus

cytisus ramentaceus.definition: erect shrub having large trifoliate leaves and dense clusters of yellow flowers followed by poisonous seeds; Yugoslavia; sometimes placed in genus Cytisus

cytisus scoparius.definition: deciduous erect spreading broom native to western Europe; widely cultivated for its rich yellow flowers
cytisus scoparius.synonyms: common broom; Scotch broom; green broom

cytoarchitectonics.definition: the cellular composition of a bodily structure

cytoarchitecture.definition: the cellular composition of a bodily structure

cytochrome.definition: (biochemistry) a class of hemoprotein whose principal biological function is electron transfer (especially in cellular respiration)

cytochrome c.definition: the most abundant and stable cytochrome; involved in energy transfer

cytogenesis.definition: the origin and development and variation of cells

cytogeneticist.definition: a geneticist who specializes in the cellular components associated with heredity

cytogenetics.definition: the branch of biology that studies the cellular aspects of heredity (especially the chromosomes)

cytogeny.definition: the origin and development and variation of cells

cytokine.definition: any of various protein molecules secreted by cells of the immune system that serve to regulate the immune system

cytokinesis.definition: organic process consisting of the division of the cytoplasm of a cell following karyokinesis bringing about the separation into two daughter cells

cytokinetic.definition: of or relating to the division of the cytoplasm of a cell following the division of the nucleus

cytokinin.definition: any of a class of plant hormones that promote cell division and delay the senescence of leaves

cytol.definition: the protoplasm of a cell excluding the nucleus; is full of proteins that control cell metabolism

cytologic.definition: of or relating to the science of cytology

cytologic smear.definition: a thin tissue or blood sample spread on a glass slide and stained for cytologic examination and diagnosis under a microscope

cytologic specimen.definition: a specimen used for cytologic examination and diagnosis

cytological.definition: of or relating to the science of cytology

cytologist.definition: a biologist who studies the structure and function of cells

cytology.definition: the branch of biology that studies the structure and function of cells

cytolysin.definition: a substance that partly or completely destroys animal cells

cytolysis.definition: pathological breakdown of cells by the destruction of their outer membrane

cytolytic.definition: of or relating to cytolysis, the dissolution or destruction of a cell

cytomegalic.definition: of or relating to or characterized by greatly enlarged cells

cytomegalovirus.definition: any of a group of herpes viruses that enlarge epithelial cells and can cause birth defects; can affect humans with impaired immunological systems

cytomembrane.definition: a thin membrane (a double layer of lipids) enclosing the cytoplasm of a cell; proteins in the membrane control passage of ions (like sodium or potassium or calcium) in and out of the cell
cytomembrane.examples: all cells have a cell membrane

cytopathogenic.definition: of or relating to or causing pathological changes in cells

cytopenia.definition: a deficiency of some cellular element of the blood

cytophilic antibody.definition: a type of antibody that has an affinity for certain kinds of cells, in addition to and unrelated to its specific affinity for the antigen that induced it, because of the properties of the Fc portion of the heavy chain.
cytophilic antibody.examples: Cytophilic antibodies are responsible for the allergic immunological response of the organism.

cytophotometer.definition: a photometer that can be used to locate and identify chemical compounds in a cell by measuring the intensity of the light that passes through stained sections of the cytoplasm

cytophotometric.definition: of or relating to the study of cells by means of a cytophotometer

cytophotometry.definition: the study of chemical compounds inside a cell by means of a cytophotometer

cytoplasm.definition: the protoplasm of a cell excluding the nucleus; is full of proteins that control cell metabolism

cytoplast.definition: the intact cytoplasmic content of a cell

cytoplastic.definition: of or relating to a cytoplast

cytosine.definition: a base found in DNA and RNA and derived from pyrimidine; pairs with guanine

cytoskeleton.definition: a microscopic network of actin filaments and microtubules in the cytoplasm of many living cells that gives the cell shape and coherence

cytosmear.definition: a thin tissue or blood sample spread on a glass slide and stained for cytologic examination and diagnosis under a microscope

cytosol.definition: the aqueous part of the cytoplasm within which various particles and organelles are suspended

cytotoxic.definition: of or relating to substances that are toxic to cells

cytotoxic drug.definition: any drug that has a toxic effect on cells; commonly used in chemotherapy to inhibit the proliferation of cancerous cells

cytotoxic t cell.definition: T cell with CD8 receptor that recognizes antigens on the surface of a virus-infected cell and binds to the infected cell and kill it
cytotoxic t cell.synonyms: killer T cell; killer cell; CD8 T cell; CD8 cell

cytotoxicity.definition: the degree to which something is toxic to living cells

cytotoxin.definition: any substance that has a toxic effect on cells

cytotropic antibody.definition: a type of antibody that has an affinity for certain kinds of cells, in addition to and unrelated to its specific affinity for the antigen that induced it, because of the properties of the Fc portion of the heavy chain.
cytotropic antibody.examples: Cytophilic antibodies are responsible for the allergic immunological response of the organism.

czar.definition:
1. a male monarch or emperor (especially of Russia prior to 1917)
2. a person having great power

czardas.definition:
1. a piece of music composed for the Hungarian Csárdás dance.
2. a piece of music in the rhythm of the Hungarian Csárdás dance.
czardas.examples:
The Csárdás is characterized by a variation in tempo: it starts out slowly (lassú) and ends in a very fast tempo (friss, literally ‘fresh’).
Classical composers who have used csárdás themes in their works include Emmerich Kálmán, Franz Liszt, Johannes Brahms, Léo Delibes, Johann Strauss, Pablo de Sarasate, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky and others.

czarina.definition: the wife or widow of a czar

czarist.definition: of or relating to or characteristic of a czar

czaristic.definition: of or relating to or characteristic of a czar

czaritza.definition: the wife or widow of a czar

czech.definition: of or relating to Czechoslovakia or its people or their language
czech.examples:
The Czech border
Czechoslovak nationalists
The Czechoslovakian population

czech.definition:
1. a native of inhabitant of the Czech Republic
2. a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia
3. the Slavic language of Czechs

czechness.definition: The quality or characteristic of being Czech.
czechness.examples: There's more Czechness in Brno than in Prague, says American academic now living in the Czech Republic.

czechoslovak.definition: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia

czechoslovakian.definition: of or relating to Czechoslovakia or its people or their language
czechoslovakian.examples:
The Czech border
Czechoslovak nationalists
The Czechoslovakian population

czechoslovakian.definition: a native or inhabitant of the former republic of Czechoslovakia

czworniak.definition: a Polish mead, made using three units of water for each unit of honey.
